Repo: /opt/nxeon-v2, branch design/v2 — a from-scratch visual redesign ("Nexion") of the real Nxeon hosting platform, running sandboxed (NXEON_SANDBOX=1: real DB and code paths, no VM ever provisions, no card ever charges). Read /opt/nxeon-v2/CLAUDE.md FIRST for the operating rules (never build in /opt/nxeon, never pkill -f by pattern, verification-by-screenshot discipline, etc). Login: customer@nxeon.local / wGPZqhCbsLdz (see /root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt), base URL https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud.

IMPORTANT — READ BEFORE STARTING: a previous attempt at this exact task got completely sidetracked and made ZERO progress on its actual assignment. It noticed a recurring `⨯ [TypeError: Invalid URL] { code: 'ERR_INVALID_URL', input: 'null' }` line in the service logs, assumed it was a login bug, and spent its entire budget chasing it (including leaving a temporary diagnostic in instrumentation.ts, which has since been reverted — do NOT re-add it). This has already been investigated for you: that error fires ~15-25 seconds after every single server restart/rebuild, completely independent of whether anyone logs in or does anything at all — it correlates with the `⚠ "next start" does not work with "output: standalone" configuration` warning that also appears on every restart, so it is almost certainly a Next.js internal quirk from how rebuild.sh starts this particular build (`next start` against a `output: standalone` build), not an application bug, and definitely not specific to login (direct manual login tests throughout this whole session have worked reliably every time). IGNORE this log line. Do not investigate it, do not add diagnostics for it, do not let it distract you. If you happen to reproduce a DIFFERENT, clearly-login-specific failure yourself (e.g., an actual failed login in your own browser session, not just this log line appearing in the background), that would be worth noting — but the log line itself, alone, is not your problem to solve.

CONTEXT — a long session just finished building a light theme for this whole dashboard (dark was the only mode before; light is new, toggled via `data-theme="light"` on `<html>`, tokens as `--color-*` CSS custom properties in app/globals.css) and found/fixed a long tail of bugs across most pages, including a broad sweep of `bg-white`/`text-white`-on-fixed-dark-surface bugs across many shared components (already done — components/customer/BackupSchedule.tsx, GameAutoUpdate.tsx, GameSettings.tsx, SslCertificates.tsx, Console.tsx, the calendar/*, claude-code/*, mail/*, gamepanel/*, freemc/* components, vpspanel/v2/kit.tsx+ui.tsx+CopyLine.tsx, and components/nx/BillingView.tsx + WhatsNewView.tsx already got a couple of `nx-dark-island` fixes on their payment-card-face/game-cover-tile visuals — check `git diff components/nx/BillingView.tsx components/nx/WhatsNewView.tsx` first thing so you know what's already been done there and don't duplicate it). You are ONE of parallel agents auditing the REMAINING, not-yet-checked pages for the same classes of bugs. COORDINATION: you may rebuild (./rebuild.sh) and restart the nxeon-v2-web service as needed for your own verification — just don't leave it down when you finish, and do NOT create git commits (the orchestrating session commits everyone's work together). Stay within your assigned pages/files (listed below).

YOUR PAGES — this is your ACTUAL assignment, not yet touched by anyone: /dashboard/billing, /dashboard/invoices, /dashboard/affiliate, /dashboard/partner, /dashboard/team, /dashboard/feedback, /dashboard/whats-new. Find each one's page component (app/dashboard/<name>/page.tsx, which will import a components/nx/<Name>View.tsx or similar — grep to find it) and any sub-tabs/modals it opens (billing in particular likely has an "add card"/"add funds" modal flow — check those too).

THE BUG TAXONOMY TO CHECK FOR ON EVERY PAGE (all of these have been found and fixed repeatedly elsewhere this session — you're checking whether the same mistakes exist on your assigned pages):
1. A literal hardcoded color (hex or rgba, e.g. `bg-[rgba(10,22,48,.5)]`, `text-[#7f9ad0]`) used for something that should adapt between themes, instead of the theme's own `--color-*` tokens / `text-tx`, `text-tx-dim`, `text-tx-faint`, `border-rim-hi`, `bg-well`, `bg-surface`, `.card`/`.card-glass`, etc. On the light page these often render as either invisible-on-invisible or a jarring leftover dark box.
2. A hero/banner section with its own fixed dark background + `text-white` heading — if it's not wrapped in the `.nx-dark-island` CSS class (also in app/globals.css), light mode's generic fix flips `text-white` to dark ink, making it invisible against a scrim that stayed dark on purpose.
3. `bg-white` (bare, not `bg-white/NN`) used to mean "always paint this literally white" (e.g. a toggle switch knob, an active-segment pill) — breaks because `--color-white` now means "ink" in light mode. Fix: literal `bg-[#fff]` if it must always be bright regardless of theme, or a proper light-mode-aware treatment.
4. An `Icon` component (components/nx/Icon.tsx) rendered with no `tone` prop inside a colored/gradient badge that has an intended contrasting text color set on the wrapper — the icon overrides that intended color with its own default tone class instead of inheriting it. Fix: `tone="inherit"`.
5. `text-white/NN` (opacity-modified) sitting on something that is NOT actually a light-mode-adapted surface — gets wrongly retargeted by the global opacity-decoupling rule meant for the actual page background.
6. Any canvas/backdrop using `globalCompositeOperation = "lighter"` or `mix-blend-screen`/`mix-blend-lighten` — washes to grey on light. Wire into components/nx/auroraTheme.ts's helpers (see components/nx/DomainsAurora.tsx for the pattern) rather than reinventing.
7. A `.card-on`-style selected state rendering as a solid dark block regardless of theme.
8. Genuine FUNCTIONAL bugs unrelated to theming — broken layout, a button that does nothing, a modal that doesn't close, text cut off, a state that never updates, real money-math looking wrong (this is a billing area — if a number looks numerically off, check the underlying calculation, don't just restyle it).

WORKFLOW: for each page, log in via a Playwright script (must live under /opt/nxeon-v2/scripts/ per CLAUDE.md, e.g. scripts/_audit_b2.mjs — delete it when done), screenshot in BOTH dark (default) and light mode (`localStorage.setItem('nx-theme','light'); document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme','light')` before navigating), actually LOOK at the screenshots (read them back as images), diagnose using the taxonomy above, fix in source, rebuild, re-screenshot to confirm, move on. Run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` after every batch of edits.

Don't invent problems that aren't there. Only fix what's actually visibly or functionally broken. Write a final report listing every bug found (short description + file) and every fix made, plus anything already correct.

content.content: # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, **stop and ask the owner first.** ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. #!/bin/bash
# Rebuild and restart the v2 sandbox.
#
# The tree runs a PRODUCTION build (`npm start`), not the dev server: ~0.8 GB
# instead of ~4.5 GB, on a box whose spare memory is measured against fifteen
# customer VMs. The cost is that nothing hot-reloads — every change needs this.
#
# WHY IT STOPS THE SERVER FIRST. `next build` writes into `.next`, which the
# running server is reading from. Building underneath a live server replaces the
# manifests it has open and every route starts returning 500 — this has already
# happened once in this tree. Stop, build, start. Never build in place.
set -euo pipefail

cd /opt/nxeon-v2
LOG=/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log

# ── one build at a time ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two concurrent runs write the same `.next` and corrupt it — the exact failure
# this script exists to prevent, arrived at from a different direction. It was
# survivable only by accident: the build runs inside a transient scope, and
# systemd refuses a second scope of the same name, so run two and the LOSER
# fails loudly. Relying on that is relying on a side effect of a name. This
# takes a real lock and says plainly what happened.
exec 9>/tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock
if ! flock -n 9; then
  echo "==> another rebuild is already running (holding /tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock)."
  echo "    Wait for it to finish — starting a second one would corrupt .next."
  exit 1
fi

# ── skip the marketing site ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The redesign does not touch marketing, but it is ~137 of the ~195 route files
# and most of the 254 static pages, so it dominates a build we now run by hand
# after every change.
#
# Next excludes any folder whose name starts with `_` from routing, so renaming
# the route group is all it takes. This is a SANDBOX-ONLY, TEMPORARY rename: the
# trap puts it back whatever happens — including a failed build or a Ctrl-C — so
# git never sees it and nothing different is ever merged to prod.
#
# Set NX_FULL=1 to build the whole site (do this before any staging/prod pass,
# where marketing MUST be built and exercised).
MK="app/(marketing)"
MK_OFF="app/_marketing_skipped"
restore() { [ -d "$MK_OFF" ] && mv "$MK_OFF" "$MK"; }
trap restore EXIT INT TERM

if [ "${NX_FULL:-0}" != "1" ] && [ -d "$MK" ]; then
  echo "==> skipping the marketing site (NX_FULL=1 to include it)"
  mv "$MK" "$MK_OFF"
fi

echo "==> stopping the server (it reads .next; building under it breaks it)"
systemctl stop nxeon-v2-web

echo "==> building"
start=$(date +%s)
# Capped so a runaway build is killed rather than squeezing the customer VMs,
# and niced so it always yields to them.
if systemd-run --scope --quiet --unit=v2-rebuild \
     -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p CPUWeight=30 \
     bash -c 'cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && export NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 && set -a && . ./.env && set +a && npm run build' \
     > "$LOG" 2>&1; then
  echo "==> built in $(( $(date +%s) - start ))s"
else
  echo "!!! BUILD FAILED — the server is NOT being restarted on a broken build."
  echo "    Last 20 lines of $LOG:"
  tail -20 "$LOG"
  exit 1
fi

  sleep 2
done

exit 1

## Summary

I audited all seven assigned pages (`/dashboard/billing`, `/dashboard/invoices` + detail, `/dashboard/affiliate`, `/dashboard/partner`, `/dashboard/team`, `/dashboard/feedback`, `/dashboard/whats-new`), including sub-tabs and modals, in both dark and light mode, using Playwright scripts under `scripts/` (all deleted when done, per policy). To exercise fuller states I created a test org ("Nexion Audit Co") and submitted two test feedback items via the real UI — harmless sandbox data.

### Bug found and fixed

**`.bar-track` hardcoded dark trough on the referral rank-progress bar** — `app/globals.css` (`.bar-track` rule, used by `components/nx/RewardsView.tsx`'s `RankCard`, which is what `/dashboard/affiliate` renders via its redirect to `/dashboard/refer`).

The progress bar's "empty" track was a literal `background: rgba(6, 16, 38, 0.66)` — a near-black fill meant for a dark page. In light mode this wasn't covered by any of the generic `bg-white/`/`rgba(10,22,48...)` retargeting selectors (it's a plain CSS class rule, not a Tailwind arbitrary-value utility on the element), so it rendered as a solid dark bar regardless of actual progress — a 0%-complete bar looked 100% full. This is the same class of bug as the already-fixed `.chip-q` pill right above it in the stylesheet (also flagged as a `/dashboard/refer` bug in an earlier pass), just missed for this specific element.

Fix: added a `html[data-theme="light"] .bar-track` override giving it a proper light neutral trough (`color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 8%, transparent)`), matching the site's established pattern. Rebuilt and re-screenshotted to confirm — the track now shows correctly empty in light mode.

### Everything else checked and already correct

- **Billing**: dashboard, Invoices/Billing settings/Usage tabs, Add funds, Redeem code, Auto-recharge, card carousel (PayPal + card faces, already `nx-dark-island`-fixed by a prior pass — confirmed via `git diff`, not duplicated), Add-card modal.
- **Invoices**: list page and invoice detail page.
- **Partner**: both the "not a partner" landing and the active partner dashboard (tested with real commission/customer data).
- **Team**: empty state, and all 5 tabs (Members/Invites/Roles & Permissions/Activity/Organisation Settings) plus the Invite Member modal (tested with a real created org).
- **Feedback**: empty state and populated list (tested with real submissions).
- **What's New**: feed, filters, stat rail; `GameCoverTile` `nx-dark-island` fix from an earlier pass confirmed correct.
- Aurora canvases (`BillingAurora`, `PartnerAurora`, `TeamAurora`, `WhatsNewAurora`) all correctly route through `auroraTheme.ts`'s theme-aware composite helper — no `lighter`/`mix-blend-screen` issues.
- No missing `Icon tone="inherit"` bugs — handled generically via CSS descendant selectors (`.chip-tone .nx-ico`, `.btn-primary .nx-ico`, etc.).
- `text-slate-*` utilities are globally retokenized via the Tailwind `@theme` block, so all the "plain" shared components (`AddFunds`, `RedeemGift`, `AutoRecharge`, `FeedbackWidget`, `InvoiceViews`, `Badge`) are already theme-safe.

### Non-bugs worth noting (not changed)

- The Invoices list/detail page formats money with a hardcoded `$`-only `fmtMoney()` (`components/ui/primitives.tsx`), while the Billing dashboard tab uses the display-currency-aware `useMoney()` hook — a real inconsistency (invoices always show `$`, billing summary shows the selected currency, e.g. `€`), but this predates the theming work and isn't a theme bug, so I left it alone.
- The sidebar "Account balance" widget shows raw USD while Billing's "Balance" stat shows the EUR-converted figure — same currency-display split, but that widget lives outside my assigned files (shared shell), so out of scope here.

### Files touched

- `/opt/nxeon-v2/app/globals.css` — added the `.bar-track` light-mode fix (one hunk; verified via `git diff` that no other unintended changes are present in this file).

Site was rebuilt and confirmed live/stable (`nxeon-v2-web` active, `/login` returns 200) before finishing.
